body:
Just tried this out. There's a few improvements that can be made I think.

There's no representation of the volume when it's occluded, seeing the bounds of the volume would be nice:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3ec28b3e-b65c-4840-884a-c6297d116e77)

The full box is obstructing and doesn't seem to provide much info. I think removing it would be fine, like we did for reflection probes and voxelGI (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100370):
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4dd42f65-4b1b-4001-88a0-742270d914e3)

Having a preview of the cell-size seems necessary, as right now there's no contex for the size of the current cells and makes this pretty cumbersome to use. I think ideally we'd see small floating transparent circles/icons where probes would be spawned. This would be nice if it was realtime, at least as long as the total amount of probes within that volume are under a certain threshold.

My initial intuition was to encapsulate my environment with the volume, however since the probes are generated on the bounds of the volume, they were placed outside. Maybe it makes sense to offset them to the inside of the volume by `cell_size/2.0`?
| Gizmo | Probes |
| - | - |
| ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b3c010b-39d2-4756-9a09-87354d081a79) | ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3098c472-732f-400f-8436-002ed6345621) |

I suspect in the end having some form of (toggleable) geometry detection would be the only proper way of improving this beyond communicating grid size ahead of baking.

Ideally probes are would be spawned more densely on geometry, and the empty space that's left is filled up with a static lower cell-size.

I think it could also be nice for probe baking to be possible on a per-probe-group basis, though I understand that'd be difficult to do right now. We'd still want a "bake all probes" option through lightmap GI.

I would also argue that with this addition, the automatic probe spawning of the LightmapGI node is obsolete, as it's not practically usable anyways as is. Is it possible to disable it when user-placed LightmapProbes are in the scene? Right now, since the best you can do is set it to "disabled", we can get probes spawning like this which is not ideal:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfab4b6c-83c9-466b-af04-004d554fea44)

I'm wondering if this might make more sense as a new node, as we cannot rename this node and something like `LightProbeGroup` seems like a more accurate description. This also opens up the opportunity separate this from lightmap baking down the line, use probes in isolation as a GI solution, and keep the possibility of spawning individual probes which is important for backwards compatibility (For people who've made their own probe spawning solutions in GDScript).

> There's no representation of the volume when it's occluded, seeing the bounds of the volume would be nice:

You can set the LightmapProbe gizmo mode to x-ray in the 3D editor's **View > Gizmos** menu at the top. Click the menu option until it becomes an half-open eye.

> The full box is obstructing and doesn't seem to provide much info. I think removing it would be fine, like we did for reflection probes and voxelGI (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100370):

Will do (I opened this PR before we tweaked the VoxelGI gizmo).

> Having a preview of the cell-size seems necessary, as right now there's no contex for the size of the current cells and makes this pretty cumbersome to use. I think ideally we'd see small floating transparent circles/icons where probes would be spawned. This would be nice if it was realtime, at least as long as the total amount of probes within that volume are under a certain threshold.

That's the idea; it should be feasible to implement by using handle gizmos (which use point rendering to draw all the points with a single draw call). The handles will be non-interactive though, but implementing this using other gizmo systems would be much more complex (and slower if it doesn't use point rendering).

> My initial intuition was to encapsulate my environment with the volume, however since the probes are generated on the bounds of the volume, they were placed outside. Maybe it makes sense to offset them to the inside of the volume by `cell_size/2.0`?

That makes sense. It'll involve reducing the actual cell size a bit (since we are bringing cells closer to each other by moving the extremities inwards), but we already do this kind of adjustments to ensure probes are evenly spaced anyway.

> Is it possible to disable it when user-placed LightmapProbes are in the scene?

That can be done, but I'm not sure we should do this automatically, even as an option. It can look confusing if you add one LightmapProbe node then automatic probe generation appears to stop all of a sudden.

> Right now, since the best you can do is set it to "disabled", we can get probes spawning like this which is not ideal:

This is done so that the LightmapGI always has valid probe data to interpolate to. If there were no probes placed at the LightmapGI's bounds, you would end up in scenarios where there is nothing to interpolate to even though the dynamic object is still within the dynamic lightmap bounds. This would lead to undefined behavior.

Maybe we could hide the 8 probes located at the edges of the LightmapGI node if it looks odd in this situation.

> and keep the possibility of spawning individual probes which is important for backwards compatibility (For people who've made their own probe spawning solutions in GDScript).

The default behavior of the node is the same as the previous behavior (it spawns a single probe), so compatibility should be 100% preserved already.

> You can set the LightmapProbe gizmo mode to x-ray in the 3D editor's View > Gizmos menu at the top. Click the menu option until it becomes an half-open eye.

True, but voxelGI and reflection probes rely on regular bounds rendering for that outline, which I think is a better approach for the case of volumes. It has x-ray by default, but still gets slightly shaded when occluded, while the gizmo-xray view loses all sense of depth.

> should be feasible to implement by using handle gizmos

This seems ideal, that's perfect!

> It can look confusing if you add one LightmapProbe node then automatic probe generation appears to stop all of a sudden.

True, I suppose the proper way to resolve this would probably be to have user placed probes take priority over lightmap generated probes, so lightmap probes don't get spawned inside user placed probe volumes like so: 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eeff5559-447b-498e-8d84-8f3a16975a57)

> you would end up in scenarios where there is nothing to interpolate to even though the dynamic object is still within the dynamic lightmap bounds.

That makes sense, hiding them could be a good option to keep things clean, though probably not very important and potentially could confuse users where they see light change without any probes being visibly present. It's probably fine to leave it as is I suppose.

> True, I suppose the proper way to resolve this would probably be to have user placed probes take priority over lightmap generated probes, so lightmap probes don't get spawned inside user placed probe volumes like so:

There's already a check in place for this in the automatic probe generator: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5e27318b6c81c7eeef462737e6259d78841757e6/scene/3d/lightmap_gi.cpp#L785-L794

It's possible that the distance defined isn't large enough though. Can you try increasing `(p_cell_size * 0.5f)` to a larger value, recompile and try baking lightmaps?

Yeah that seemed to be the case:
| 0.5 | 2.0 |
| - | - |
| ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5dbe8827-b71e-40bd-93d3-07bdef096ba8) | ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76dd50b9-001d-4a09-a5fe-bcc08d033a62) |

In my eyes this is more of an issue with the "subdivision" based probe placement (as opposed to letting the user define a grid size for probe placement) in the LightmapGI node.

This merging system doesn't consider manually placed probes though, I don't know if that is desired and if we'd even want to mitigate that (I feel like we shouldn't mess with user placed probes at all, except maybe when there are overlapping volumes it makes sense to just give priority to the one with the smallest cell size?), but definitely something to be aware of:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4227e731-16eb-4cc6-b663-95b7e53dd4e9)

In that specific scenario it probably shouldn't even get rid of it, as it's a corner probe, but I feel like it would make sense for the automatic spawning to purge any probes (Except the corners) that are placed within a user placed probe volume.
